The '''2016–17 [[Super League Greece]]''' was the 81st season of the highest tier in league of [[Football in Greece|Greek]] [[Association football|football]] and the eleventh under its current title. The season started on 10 September 2016 and ended in June 2017. The league comprised fourteen teams from the 2015–16 season and two promoted from the [[2015–16 Football League (Greece)|2015–16 Football League]].

==Teams==
Two teams were relegated from the [[2015–16 Super League Greece|2015–16 season]]. [[Panthrakikos F.C.|Panthrakikos]] and [[AEL Kalloni F.C.|AEL Kalloni]] would play in [[Football League (Greece)|Football League]] for the 2016–17 season.

Two teams were promoted from the [[2015–16 Football League (Greece)|2015–16 Football League]], champions [[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]] and [[PAE Kerkyra|Kerkyra]].

=== Postponement  ===
The Greek Super League was originally scheduled for 20 August 2016 but Greece's Sports minister [[Stavros Kontonis]] decided it would be postponed due to fears of violence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com.au/greek-super-league/story/2932462/greek-super-league-delayed-at-least-two-weeks-over-fears-of-violence|title=Greek Super League delayed|date=18 August 2016}}</ref>

The first match was then postponed and scheduled to be played on 10 September 2016 between [[PAE Kerkyra|Kerkyra]] and [[Platanias F.C.|Platanias]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soccerway.com/greece/super-league-2016-2017/results/|title=Summary - Super League 1 - Greece - Results, fixtures, tables and news - Soccerway|website=Soccerway}}</ref>

The match was a success and went ahead with no issues with [[Platanias F.C.|Platanias]] winning 1–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/match/2355591/kerkyra-vs-platanias/report|title=Kerkyra vs Platanias (SBS)|access-date=23 September 2016}}</ref>

On 9 November refereeing chief Giorgos Bikas was the victim of an arson attack, this led to Greek football of all divisions to be suspended.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/nov/09/greece-suspend-football-arson-attack-refereeing-chief|title=Greece suspend football competitions after arson attack on refereeing chief|date=9 November 2016}}</ref>

==Play-offs==
In the play-offs for Champions League and Europa League berths, the four qualified teams play each other in a home and away [[Round-robin tournament|round robin]]. However, they do not all start with 0 points. Instead, a weighting system applies to the teams' standing at the start of the play-off mini-league. The team finishing fifth in the Super League will start the play-off with 0 points. The fifth placed team's end of season tally of points is subtracted from the sum of the points that other teams have. This number is then divided by five.

So, both AEK Athens and Panionios will begin the play-offs pointless. PAOK will enter the play-offs with two points, while Panathinaikos will have one point.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://greece.greekreporter.com/2017/05/02/paok-and-panathinaikos-score-leading-edge-over-aek-and-panionios-ahead-of-play-offs/|title = PAOK and Panathinaikos Score Leading Edge over AEK and Panionios Ahead of Play-offs|date = 2 May 2017}}</ref>

==Attendances==
